action.question: How should an analysis carry the session-vs-manager split? Your feedback examples (e.g. #66: "write notes, create a ticket, then close the thread") mix session-facing and manager-facing steps in one situation.

questions.question: How should an analysis carry the session-vs-manager split? Your feedback examples (e.g. #66: "write notes, create a ticket, then close the thread") mix session-facing and manager-facing steps in one situation.

options.label: Two recs per analysis
options.description: Each analysis produces up to a session-rec (sent to the session) AND a manager-rec (executed by claude -p); either may be empty. Matches 'do X in-session, then I'll close it' sequences. More UI/data but most faithful.

options.label: One targeted rec
options.description: Each analysis yields a single recommendation tagged TARGET=session|manager. Simpler; a mixed situation needs a re-analyze or picks the dominant action.

questions.question: How should a manager-targeted rec actually get executed by claude -p?

options.label: Human-authorized, gated off
options.description: Operator clicks 'run as manager' in the UI to spawn the claude -p; behind a new flag (e.g. MANAGER_EXECUTE_ENABLED, default off) mirroring submit_enabled's shadow→review→flip. Until enabled it shows the exact command/prompt it would run.

options.label: Auto-run in the loop
options.description: The monitor loop spawns the executor claude -p automatically once a manager-rec matures past grace (full autonomous shepherd). Higher blast radius.
